q: How do I calculate the carbon footprint of an electric kettle?
title: Electric kettle carbon footprint
short: Weigh the stainless steel or plastic body, heating element, base, cord and controls, and multiply each by its supplier's figure. Add pressing, moulding, assembly and testing energy per unit and the carton. Metals and plastics are usually most of the total.

ul: Stainless steel or PP body and lid.
Power base, cord, plug and connectors.
Deep drawing or moulding of the body.

p: Report cradle to gate per kettle. Use-phase electricity is usually larger over its life, so state it separately if asked.

example.title: Worked example: kettle assembly per unit (one month)
lines: Plant total: 14,200 / 40,000 = 0.355 kg CO2 per kettle
Add steel, plastics, element and cord for the full figure
example.note: Inputs are illustrative; use your own bills and production records.

senseible: Senseible reads the plant's electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and fuel invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record, the plant-level input to a per-unit figure. Bought-in materials go to the supplier evidence trail; product reports are self-declared drafts.
